arrangement: A public DNS name that resolves to an AWS Network Load Balancer with instance targets (the cluster's worker nodes) across three Availability Zones; the F5 NGINX Ingress Controller running in the cluster; one Ingress rule for host shop.example.com and path /cart pointing at a Service named cart; three pods behind that Service. NGINX balances directly to pod addresses, which is that controller's default.

claims.text: A Network Load Balancer has a DNS name that resolves to the IP addresses of its load balancer nodes, one per enabled Availability Zone; AWS removes a zone's address from DNS when that zone has no healthy target.

claims.text: An Ingress does nothing by itself; an ingress controller such as NGINX fulfils the rules.

A Service is an abstraction that gives a set of pods one stable name and virtual IP address; the virtual IP is implemented by rules that kube-proxy programs on each node, not by a process listening on that address.

steps.text: The browser resolves the name to the load balancer's addresses.
The load balancer forwards to a healthy node.
NGINX matches host and path to an Ingress rule that names a Service.
NGINX chooses one of the pods behind that Service and sends the request to it.
